timeline.description: DFT structural relaxation (PBE, 520 eV cutoff, 7x7x7 k-grid) of 1317 antiperovskite compositions.

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper explicitly states that the antiperovskite compositional space examined totals 1317 compounds (“for a total number of compounds under examination of 1317”) and describes DFT structural relaxations using VASP with PBE, an energy cutoff of 520 eV, and a 7×7×7 k-point grid for unit cells. These statements appear in the “Workflow” and “Structural relaxations” sections (Pages 2–3).

timeline.description: Antiperovskite structure check based on geometric criteria (unit cell angles, lengths, X–A/B distances, octahedral angles).

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper explicitly describes an “Antiperovskite structure check” as the first filtering criterion after structural relaxation. It states the check is based on geometric criteria: (1) unit cell angles near 90° (±2°), (2) unit cell lengths within 0.5 Å of each other, (3) X–A distances within 0.5 Å of each other, (4) X–B distances within 0.5 Å of each other, and (5) octahedral angles near 90° (±13°). This matches the extracted value’s description of a structure check based on unit cell angles/lengths, X–A/B distances, and octahedral angles (workflow step/timeline).

timeline.description: Thermodynamic stability assessment via energy above convex hull (<0.2 eV/atom).

_llm_flag.reasoning: The paper explicitly states under the “Thermodynamic stability” section that stability is assessed via energy above the convex hull, and that the criterion is relaxed to include compounds with an energy above the hull of less than 0.2 eV/at (i.e., per atom) due to DFT inaccuracies/metastability. This matches the extracted workflow timeline statement.

The paper explicitly states under the “Electronic properties” section that PBE is used to determine the band gap and that “a cut-off band gap of 0.5 eV is used” to filter materials (i.e., band gap threshold ≥0.5 eV). This corresponds to an electronic property filter of bandgap ≥0.5 eV (PBE).

timeline.description: Electrochemical stability window computed with Grand Potential Phase Diagrams; requirement ≥1 V.

_llm_flag.reasoning: Page 4 explicitly states that the Electrochemical Stability Window (ESW) is determined using Grand Potential Phase Diagrams (GPPDs) and that a minimal ESW of 1 V is chosen as the passing/requirements criterion (“A minimal ESW of 1 V is chosen as the passing criteria… compounds with an ESW smaller than 1 V are rejected.”).
